correctness.rationale: For m=∫F finite and R₀=∫A>1 the constant equilibrium and exact perturbation equation yield H=A/R₀−(R₀−1)F/m and Δ=1−Ĥ. For σ≥0, g=e^(−σa)F is integrable, decreasing and distributionally convex since F′=−K is nondecreasing. Both g and its right derivative tend to zero at infinity, so g(a)=∫(u−a)_+dg′(u). Tonelli gives ∫u² dg′(u)=2∫g<∞, justifying the cosine transform identity with nonnegative integrand (1−cos(ωu))/ω² after integration. The normalized positive A term has real part strictly less than one except at z=0: for σ>0 the maximal weight is attained only at a=0, and for nonzero ω on the axis it is attained only on a null set. At z=0, Δ=R₀−1>0. This establishes strict positivity of the determinant's real part throughout the claimed half-plane. With an exponential moment, monotonicity bounds e^(ηa)F(a) for a≥1 by e^η∫_(a−1)^a e^(ηs)F(s)ds; thus A=βF also has an exponential moment. For bounded real parts the exponentially weighted kernels range over a compact L¹ set, so Riemann–Lebesgue decay is uniform there; large positive real parts give small transform directly by domination. Compactness on the remaining bounded rectangle extends nonvanishing to Re z≥−δ for a sufficiently small δ>0. The weighted causal Wiener criterion then gives an inverse identity plus an L¹(e^(δa)da) resolvent. Splitting at t=0, each G in {H,F,A} contributes a past forcing bounded in weighted sup norm by ||G||_(1,δ)||history||_∞. Causal convolutions have the same operator bound on future perturbations, and the weighted norm of a product is at most the product of weighted norms. The resulting resolvent fixed-point map on a ball of radius proportional to the history size is a contraction for small compatible histories; it gives exponential incidence decay. No decay of the entire past in the unweighted history norm is asserted. The uniform-duration illustration is Uniform[0,T], as confirmed by the supplied cosine check, not a uniform distribution starting at a positive age.
residual_risks: Without an exponential moment only the characteristic-root exclusion is proved, not an exponential rate or a nonlinear global claim.
Closed-right-half-plane exclusion rules out a classical Hopf crossing; it is not a classification of every form of nonlinear or infinite-memory dynamics.

evidence: Nakata–Röst gives local and global endemic stability with constant transmission and a finite maximum infectious period.
Their discussion cites Gripenberg for a variable-infectivity integral equation with technical assumptions on infectivity and sojourn kernels; the underlying article was not recovered.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For zero mortality the first comparison fits the target by taking a constant profile on the support of F and zero outside, which is L¹ for finite support. Its stronger stability conclusion on that case does not extend the infectivity quantifier. The secondary Gripenberg description is too imprecise to decide coverage and is a residual risk.

evidence: Same-model determinant is already derived in Scarabel et al.; Nakata–Röst's proof specializes to constant transmission. Diekmann–Montijn obtains Fourier-coefficient conditions for crossings of a different determinant.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Deriving the determinant, or proving an exclusion for one transmit-profile family, does not yield the required right-half-plane estimate uniform over every admissible profile. The main extra step is to apply classical convex-kernel cosine positivity to the survival term and independently bound the real part of the normalized positive profile. General linearized stability machinery supplies a method once the zero-free region has been proved, not that region itself.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected paper has the identical renewal model and determinant, but its checked analysis does not state this profile-uniform sufficient condition. Earlier constant-transmission results give stronger convergence for a special model, not this quantifier. The Fourier positivity argument for decreasing convex integrable kernels and the causal resolvent method are classical techniques; the supported contribution is the exact application to the endemic determinant for every admissible nonnegative age profile, and the local incidence consequence with light tails. Unavailable sources are reported as limits, not negative evidence.
residual_risks: Gripenberg's exact kernel hypotheses and Chen–Yang–Zhang's full theorem were not recovered; broader coverage may be found there or in other general renewal literature.
A broader web lookup was unavailable and adds no evidence of noncoverage. The judgment rests on the actual sources compared.

value.rationale: A single test on the shape of the survival law replaces a separate search for characteristic roots for each admissible age profile. It gives an analytic boundary for classical endemic Hopf behavior in the same model studied via specific bifurcation examples, and separates the root exclusion from the stronger incidence convergence available only with a tail hypothesis. This usefulness does not depend on a new Fourier or Wiener theorem.
residual_risks: The shape restriction is sufficient only, and neither global convergence nor a converse follows.
